tb-101-4.question:
The graph below shows how the length L of a liquid column of a liquid-in-glass thermometer varies with temperature T (Fig a).

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) L does not change linearly with T within this temperature range.

(2) L is less than 11 cm when T is 50 °C.

(3) T is lower than 14.3 °C when L is 6 cm.

A (1) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-101-4.reasoning:
Consider the points on a straight line passing through (0, 4) and (100, 18).

When T = 50 °C,

50-0100-0 = L-418-4

L = 11 cm

When T = 50 °C, the value of L of the point on the given graph is less than that on the straight line, i.e. is less than 11 cm.

∴ (2) is correct.

Consider the points on the straight line again.

When L = 6 cm,

T-0100-0 = 6-418-4

T = 14.3 °C

When L = 6 cm, the value of T of the point on the given graph is higher than that on the straight line, i.e. is higher than 14.3 °C.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-101-7.question:
Winnie wants to measure the temperature of warm water with a resistance thermometer. Before the measurement, she puts the thermometer in a bowl of pure melting ice for calibration (Fig b).

(a) State one precaution during calibration. (1 mark)

(b) Which property does the resistance thermometer make use of to measure temperature? How does this property change with temperature? (2 marks)
tb-101-7.answer:
(a) Avoid the tip of the thermometer from touching the bowl when taking reading. 1A

(b) It makes use of the electrical resistance of metal to measure temperature. 1A

Electrical resistance increases with temperature. 1A

tb-101-8.question:
A thermometer using infra-red thermography is installed in a commercial buildings to check visitors’ body temperatures (Fig c). The thermometer takes the images of visitors with a camera and their images are shown on a monitor as colour patches. Different colours indicate different intensities of infra-red radiation emitted by the visitors.

(a) Which temperature-dependent property does the thermometer use? How does this property change with temperature? (2 marks)

(b) Suggest two benefits in using the infra-red thermometer to measure visitors’ body temperature during a pandemic. (2 marks)
tb-101-8.answer:
(a) It makes use of the intensity of infra-red radiation to measure temperature. 1A

Part with a higher temperature emits infra-red radiation of a higher intensity. 1A

(b) The result is shown almost instantaneously. 1A

No direct contact to the visitors is needed. 1A

tb-101-9.question:
X is a resistance thermometer. Figure d shows how its resistance R change with temperature T.

Figure d: the temperature tick to the left of 0 corresponds to −100 °C.

(a) Find the temperature when R = 80 Ω. (1 mark)

(b) Calculate the resistance when the temperature is −30 °C. Assume R varies linearly with T even when T is negative. (2 marks)

(c) Y is another resistance thermometer. Figure e shows how its resistance R change with temperature T.

State a disadvantage of Y compared with X in measuring temperature. (1 mark)
tb-101-9.answer:
(a) 180 °C 1A

(b) When T = 180 °C, R = 80 Ω

When T = 0 °C, R = 20 Ω

0-(-30)180-0 = 20-R80-20 1M

R = 10 Ω 1A

(c) The resistance of Y shows linear relation with temperature within a smaller range of temperature. 1A

tb-101-11.answer:

= 0.0749 − 0.0735

= 0.0001 cm2
